rv.q: Held aloft by a buoyant beat, this show couldn’t be a more welcome message right now.
That seamlessness is The Heart’s great advantage and its disappointment.
The Heart is all of a piece, a unique and profoundly emotional story for which the right style, the right words, and the right music all come together.
Performed and staged with Broadway-level excellence, The Heart is a remarkable musical drama well worth seeing.
The musical form is stronger for all of Sondheim’s experimentation, and because of him we now have wonderful shows like “The Heart,” which opened Thursday at Roundabout’s Laura Pels Theatre.
“The Heart” could become one of the most memorable and awarded new musicals of the Main Stem season.
The Eisendraths’ high-voltage thrums are an ingenious match for the musical medical procedural.
The subject matter should be no obstacle to your enjoyment of this neatly produced and dramatically rich new offering.

At times, and increasingly over its 90 minutes, it succeeds. And at other times, you a) ponder the miscalculations on that stage in both the writing and the execution, b) do some mental rewriting, and c) plug your ears, because gosh, is it loud.
There’s something very cold about The Heart, though I respect the musical’s ambition as a constantly pulsing poperetta.
The Heart is a remarkable, pulse-pounding achievement, as inventive as it is moving.
It promises to be one of the most powerful productions of the New York season.
Over the course of a swift ninety minutes, it might just make your heart skip a beat.
With a club-ready score, an ER’s sense of urgency, and a cast that never misses a cue, The Heart asks for a little suspended disbelief and pays it forward by the final heartbeat.
The Heart has the look and feel of a show that drives forward with narrative momentum, but there’s a hollowness to the material that could benefit from a consult with a skilled cardiologist.

cn.t: Critics largely embrace this ambitious organ-transplant musical for its bold subject matter, electropop score, and emotional punch, though some find it cold or uneven. Most praise its contemporary urgency and expert execution.

vr.q: It's funny, moving, and a really cool celebration of life and modern medicine.
